payload.feature:
This worktree carries the verifier and shipper as boxed exec gates (decision 0043's consequence, decision 0041 ruling 2's roster row) as delivered by run decision-0043-docs-decisions-004-29528051: commits de7248a, c08c8d4 and 923ecbd on top of main aa9394c. That run reforged twice — its first review caught a real hole, a commit id steered into a ledger `--output` path under .git/hooks, closed fail-closed in c08c8d4 — and then parked at REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-MEDIUM with two MEDIUM correctness findings standing. The run is concluded; this slice answers exactly those two findings on top of the existing commits and ships. Keep every property the three commits established: the two scripts and their contract, the `brokkr ledger` verb with its argument guards, the boxed sites, the retired verifier and shipper agents, the mixed-panel compile refusal, the roster pins.

Finding 1, quoted from the review: "crates/brokkr-cli/tests/hands.rs this_workspaces_verifier_passes_inside_its_real_box runs the entire workspace suite inside a box and terminates only because can_create_namespace() fails for the copy of itself that runs inside that box. That is a property of this host, not of the product: .github/workflows/ci.yml explicitly sets apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0 and unprivileged_userns_clone=1 on both the test job and the required coverage job, where nested bubblewrap will very likely succeed, so the inner cargo test re-runs this test, which opens another box, up to the kernel's nesting depth, each level a full suite, under a 20-minute job timeout. Even without recursion the coverage job builds the workspace a second time cold inside the box." Fix: the box sets an explicit in-box marker the engine owns (an environment entry set by `box_argv`, for example `BROKKR_HANDS_BOX=1`, documented in the hands module), every test that opens a box skips itself when the marker is set, and the in-box verifier test drives a small, named suite rather than the whole workspace — a scratch crate with one passing and one failing test, as the framing asked — so the test proves the box and the contract without rebuilding the workspace inside itself. Say in the test's comment why nesting is refused by marker and not by a kernel accident.

Finding 2, quoted: "The exec commands name scripts by a path relative to the workdir (bash recipes/node/roles/verify-seat.sh; bash scripts/verify-seat.sh), and the box binds only the worktree plus declared toolchain dirs, never the bundle roots. recipes/node/README.md says to run with --repo /path/to/your-node-repo, but that repository holds no recipes/node/roles/verify-seat.sh, so the verify seat exits 127 with no result file. Same for brokkr init my-bundle and for recipes/fast on any Rust repository but this one. The previous model verifier worked in a foreign repo because its charter rode in the prompt." The ruling this enactment makes, grounded in what the bundle already is: a script is part of the strategy, not of the repository, so it travels with the bundle. The recipe-authoring guide already says a `./`-prefixed argv entry is bundle-relative and expanded at spawn; the fix is to make that expansion reach inside the box: `brokkr hands exec` binds the bundle's root read-only into the namespace at a fixed path and expands `./`-prefixed entries against it, so `["{brokkr}", "driver", "exec", "--", "bash", "./scripts/verify-seat.sh", "{prompt_file}"]` runs the bundle's own script from inside the box whatever repository the run works in. Every shipped recipe's verify and ship seats, bundles/self, bundles/verify and the init scaffold name their scripts that way; the manifest keeps recording driver names, never resolved paths. Pin it: a hands test runs a boxed exec seat whose script lives outside the worktree and asserts it executed; a test that a `./` entry in an exec site resolves against the bundle root inside the box; recipes/node's and preflight's README lines about running against a foreign repository stay true, and the adoption guide's walk needs no copying step. Say in the hands module's doc comment that the bundle root is bound read-only and why.

Constraints: the exact coverage gate (scripts/coverage-exact.sh, run with stdin closed: </dev/null) must stay at literal 100% and must not recurse into a box; clippy -D warnings and fmt must stay clean; cargo test --workspace green on Linux with box-building tests cfg(target_os = "linux"); contracts/, fixtures/ and policy/phase-machine.json are read-only and this slice needs no contract change; the decision index docs/decisions/README.md must keep every row main carries in number order; do not name the private neighbours in prose; keep the CLI list "claude, codex or dsh" whenever a list of harnesses appears; commit in the repository's style on top of 923ecbd and never push.

result.notes: Closed both review findings: hands boxes now mark and refuse nested box-building tests explicitly, verifier coverage uses a tiny named scratch suite, and exec gates mount their owning bundle read-only at /runtime/bundle so bundle-relative scripts run against foreign worktrees. Updated all shipped gate argv, scaffold output, docs, regression tests and manifest witnesses; fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, and exact 100% coverage all pass. Committed as ff45ebe.

cargo test --workspace: 57 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed ff45ebe (on de7248a..923ecbd over main aa9394c) for correctness, simplicity and security; changed nothing, committed nothing. Finding 1 of the prior review is closed as framed: box_argv sets BROKKR_HANDS_BOX=1 after --clearenv (hands.rs:307-310, pinned in the argv test), every box-opening test skips on the marker through can_create_namespace (protocol hands/tests.rs:14, cli tests/hands.rs:34, cli src/tests.rs:3043; no unguarded bwrap-spawning test remains), the whole-workspace-in-a-box test is gone and the verifier is proven on a two-test scratch crate with a FAIL toggle, the module doc and the test comment say why the marker and not the kernel refuses nesting. Finding 2 is enacted in the engine correctly (hands_command binds one root at /runtime/bundle and rewrites root-prefixed argv; --bundle-root on hands exec; docs and READMEs updated; manifest still records names) but the recipes were not made to match it, which is a new HIGH.

FINDINGS, none fixed (read-only seat):

(1) HIGH correctness — bundles/self, bundles/verify, recipes/fast, ember, crucible, night-shift, panel-review, sdd (verify and ship) and recipes/node (ship) now name `./scripts/verify-seat.sh` / `./scripts/ship-seat.sh`. A `./` entry is expanded by expand_command against the layer that wrote it (bundle.rs:751 and :1972: dir.join(rel), dir = the bundle root), so these resolve to `<root>/scripts/…`; no such directory exists under any of those roots (`ls bundles/*/scripts recipes/*/scripts` — none), the two scripts live only at the repository root `scripts/`. hands_command then rewrites the path to /runtime/bundle/scripts/verify-seat.sh, bash exits 127 inside the box, no result file is written, the seat fails, retries once and parks. Every self-forge run and every Rust recipe's verify and ship gate is broken on every repository including this one; only recipes/node's and recipes/preflight's verify seats (`./roles/verify-seat.sh`, files present) resolve. It fails closed (never a false pass), so correctness not security. This run's own verify seat passed only because the run's pinned bundle predates ff45ebe and the installed engine ran the old `bash scripts/verify-seat.sh` relative to the worktree; the new argv was never executed against a shipped bundle. The machine-proof test copies the scripts into its scratch bundle's scripts/ (tests/hands.rs:511-521), which is exactly what the shipped bundles lack. Fix: give every bundle root its scripts (bundles/self/scripts, bundles/verify/scripts, recipes/fast/scripts, recipes/node/scripts and the five recipes that carry their own exec sites — or have those extend fast's seats so the script lives once) and pin existence.

(2) MEDIUM test-coverage — the gap that let (1) through: the roster pin (tests/roster.rs:239-247) strips the root and compares only the tail `scripts/verify-seat.sh`, never `is_file()`; the in-box proof (tests/hands.rs:186-215) passes an already-absolute `/runtime/bundle/outside.sh` rather than a `./` entry through compile → hands_command → box; an_exec_seat_with_hands_is_boxed_whole checks the string rewrite only. The framing asked for a test that a `./` entry in an exec site resolves against the bundle root inside the box; none compiles a shipped bundle and runs its exec site. Add `assert!(Path::new(&command[5]).is_file())` to the roster pin and one boxed run of a compiled exec site.

(3) LOW correctness — with the marker, any coverage measured inside a box is permanently short of 100% because every box-building test skips there; recipes/preflight/roles/verify-seat.sh runs `bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh` inside its box, so preflight's verifier now fails deterministically on this repository. Pre-existing on this host (nested bwrap was already refused) and the framing's constraint is met outside the box (the seats' logs and the prior reviews measured 100% there), but it needs a ruling: run the coverage gate outside the box, or say preflight is not for this repository.

(4) INFO security — BROKKR_HANDS_BOX is an ordinary environment variable: an implementer could set it through `.cargo/config.toml [env]` and every box test would skip silently in CI. The exact coverage gate would then go red on the uncovered box paths and the diff is visible to review, so no exploit path; worth an `unset` or an assertion in the coverage job.

(5) INFO simplicity — the docker confinement path already binds every bundle root read-only at its own host path (engine.rs:2905-2908), which needs no argv rewriting; the hands path binds one root at a fixed mount and rewrites argv. The framing ruled the fixed mount, so this is noted for the asymmetry only; a composed bundle whose one exec command names scripts from two layers would bind only the first matching root.

(6) INFO — `brokkr hands exec --bundle-root` taken relative: bwrap runs with cwd `/` (hands.rs:789) so the source is not found and the box refuses; fails closed, undocumented.

Standing LOWs from the previous review, outside this slice's framing and unchanged: script bytes enter no manifest digest (narrowed now that a foreign-repo bundle is not implementer-writable, still open for bundles/self); the roster pin asserts neither network:false nor the ~/.cargo credential mask; bundles/self/shipper.md and recipes/fast/shipper.md are orphaned; init's verify_script runs commands through `bash -lc`.

Gates from this seat at ff45ebe: cargo fmt --check clean (.forge/review3-fmt.log); clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings clean (.forge/review3-clippy.log); tests/hands (8), init_stacks (16), roster (8), witness_digests (3) all ok (.forge/review3-test.log) — the box-building hands tests skip in this seat's sandbox, which cannot create a namespace, so their bodies were not exercised here; the implementer and verify seat report them green. Exact coverage not re-measured from this seat: the verdict does not turn on it and the script is denied to a seat. Decision index, contracts/, fixtures/, policy/phase-machine.json untouched by the delivery; no harness list added to prose; docs' claims about foreign repositories are true of the engine but false of the shipped bundles until (1) lands.

Closed the returned HIGH and MEDIUM findings in commit 15457c0: every shipped exec-gate bundle root now carries the exact verifier or shipper script it references, the roster proves resolved scripts are files, and a Linux integration test compiles and executes a shipped bundle against a worktree with no scripts directory. cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, and exact 100% coverage all pass locally; no push performed.

Reviewed ff45ebe and 15457c0 on top of 923ecbd for correctness, simplicity and security. Both standing findings are answered: (1) box_argv sets BROKKR_HANDS_BOX after --clearenv, every box-opening test (protocol hands/tests.rs, cli src/tests.rs, cli tests/hands.rs) skips on the marker before probing bwrap, and the in-box verifier test drives a scratch crate with one passing and one failing test instead of the workspace; the test comment says nesting is refused by marker, not by kernel accident. (2) brokkr hands exec takes --bundle-root, box_argv ro-binds it at /runtime/bundle, hands_command finds the bundle root that owns an argv entry (so inherited seats of composed recipes bind the layer that wrote them) and remaps that entry under /runtime/bundle; every shipped verify/ship site, bundles/self, bundles/verify and the init scaffold use ./ entries; the roster test asserts the resolved script exists and is bundle-relative in source; hands.rs integration tests run a script outside the worktree via --bundle-root and drive bundles/verify against a foreign scratch repo to the VERIFY-FAIL stop (exit 3, which a missing script cannot produce: no result parks at exit 2). Manifest records driver names only. Journal stays read-only for ship; ledger guards untouched; contracts/, fixtures/, policy/phase-machine.json and the decision index untouched; no harness lists added. cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo test --workspace green per the verify seat. NOT VERIFIED: scripts/coverage-exact.sh could not be run from this seat (sandbox refused the command) and the verify seat did not run it; from the delta every new branch and closure in hands_command, box_argv and the CLI verb is exercised by unit tests, so I expect the gate to hold but it is unproven here. RESIDUALS (none fixed, none above low): [LOW, correctness] the verify-seat.sh shipped by recipes/fast, ember, crucible, night-shift, sdd and panel-review still runs `cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self`, so on any Rust repository other than this one the script now runs but the gate reports fail; recipes/fast/README declares this and the framing preserved the scripts, so low; the test scratch crate is named brokkr-cli with an empty bundles/self dir to satisfy exactly this coupling. [LOW, simplicity] the verifier and shipper exist as nine byte-identical copies under bundle roots plus a tenth pair at scripts/ that no bundle runs; the hands tests exercise the scripts/ copies while runs execute the bundle copies, and only witness digest re-pins would surface drift between them. [INFO] the hands module doc says the mount keeps the script from becoming writable project input; for bundles/self the root lies inside the rw worktree bind, so a boxed gate can still edit it through the worktree path (pre-existing exposure, covered by review of the patch map). [INFO] hands_command remaps by path prefix rather than by ./ origin, so when a bundle root contains the workdir, {prompt_file} and {brokkr} are also remapped onto the read-only mount; harmless today. [INFO, security] the in-box marker is an environment variable, so a host shell exporting BROKKR_HANDS_BOX silently greens every box test, the same silent-skip shape as the pre-existing no-bwrap case; the marker never affects the box boundary itself. No security finding above info.
